title: The Last Bridge
premise: In the waning months of a grinding war, Cyrus Sandoval serves as a battlefield nurse at a river crossing where the last intact bridge determines who escapes and who is left behind. Keeping a private ledger of the wounded and dead that officers omit from official reports, Cyrus believes record-keeping is the only loyalty that matters—until a sealed letter arrives naming their found family of orderlies and stretcher-bearers as conspirators in a plot to sabotage the bridge. As evacuation orders come and one berth remains on the morning ship, Cyrus must expose the truth in the ledger to clear their family's names, knowing the revelation will condemn a beloved comrade instead. In the end, Cyrus gives the berth away, stays behind with the ledger, and burns the bridge themselves so no more names need be added.
about_author: Tamsin Nakamura is the pen name of a former triage nurse who spent a decade collecting oral histories from wartime medics before turning to fiction. They write about the people history forgets to count.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Establishes the field hospital at Harrow's Crossing and the ledger Cyrus keeps hidden in a ammunition crate—names the officers strike from reports. Introduces the found family: gruff orderly Beckett, young runner Odile, and surgeon's assistant Maren. Emotional beat: quiet defiance disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Sealed Letter
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A courier delivers a sealed letter addressed to 'the household of the crossing,' naming Beckett, Odile, and Maren as parties to a plot against the bridge. Cyrus hides it but cannot unlearn its contents. Emotional beat: the sickening shift from observer to participant.

chapters.title: Orders Come at Dusk
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Evacuation orders arrive: one transport berth per unit, ship sails on the morning tide in six days. The family celebrates prematurely; Cyrus says nothing about the letter. Emotional beat: guilt curdling beneath borrowed joy.

chapters.title: Ledger Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus cross-references the letter against ledger entries and discovers the plot is real—but orchestrated by someone inside the hospital, someone whose omissions they've recorded for months. Emotional beat: the horror that truth-keeping has made them complicit by silence.

chapters.title: Beckett's Hands
chapters.summary: Beckett's POV. Flashbacks interwoven with present duty reveal Beckett's brother was executed after a bridge collapse he didn't cause; his rage at officers explains his proximity to the plotters without proving guilt. Emotional beat: sympathy deepening suspicion.

chapters.title: The Berth Question
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The family argues over who takes the single berth; each volunteers another. Odile, sixteen and lying about her age, quietly decides it must be her so the others can keep working. Emotional beat: love expressed as self-erasure.

chapters.title: What Officers Omit
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. An officer demands Cyrus surrender all records; Cyrus refuses and is threatened with arrest. The confrontation forces Cyrus to realize the ledger can either save their family or destroy Beckett—not both. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth pulling apart like rope under load.

chapters.title: The Plot at Low Water
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The saboteurs move at low tide; Maren catches them rigging charges and is wounded warning the others. Beckett arrives and stops the detonation, but the officer credits himself and names Beckett as ringleader anyway. Emotional beat: heroism punished by the machinery of blame.

chapters.title: The Last Bridge
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, climax. At dawn, with the ship whistling and soldiers swarming, Cyrus reads the ledger aloud to the assembled command—the true names, the true plot, the officer's omissions. It clears Beckett and condemns Cyrus to stay behind as witness. Emotional beat: truth spoken at last, at full cost.

chapters.title: Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, resolution. Odile takes the last berth only because Cyrus presses the ledger into her hands—'carry the names.' From the ship she watches Cyrus and Beckett fire the bridge themselves so the retreat ends cleanly and no one else is left waiting. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance; the ledger sails on when its keeper cannot.
